turns.teacher: Ok so, do you know what the sum of the angles in any quadrilateral is?

A quadrilateral is any four sided shape, so like a square, rectangle, parallelogram or kite, which this one is
and the angles inside a quadrilateral always add up to 360 degrees

we know that two of the angle in this quadrilateral are 150 and 60 degrees
if we take those angles away from 360, then that will tell us how much is left for the other two angles
360 - 150 - 60 = 150
So the other two angles together add up to 150 degrees
Happy so far?

Great
Now, those little lines on the side of the kite means that the two shorter sides are both the same length, and the two longer sides are both the same length
which means that a kite is symmetrical - we can chop it in half and the two sides are mirror images of each other
in this case, we could draw a line of symmetry horizontally across the kite, going through the angles of 150 and 60 degrees
Okay with that?

Great
So what that also tells us, is that the angle p and the angle that hasn't been labelled are the same - because the kite is symmetrical
so together those two angles add up to 150 degrees and they're both the same
which means we can divide 150 in half to work out how many degrees each angle is
150 / 2 = 75
so both p and the other angle that isn't labelled are 75 degrees each
Are you happy with all that?

Question Text: Which of the following best describes how to construct a triangle with side lengths \( 7 \mathrm{~cm} \) and \( 6 \mathrm{~cm} \), with an angle of \( 40^{\circ} \) in between?
Answer A Text: - Draw a line \( 7 \mathrm{~cm} \) long
- Place a protractor at one end of the line, measure \( 40^{\circ} \) and place a dot
- Draw a line \( 6 \mathrm{~cm} \) long that starts at the same end of the line and goes through the dot.
- Join up the end of this line with the other end of the \( 7 \mathrm{~cm} \) line.
Answer B Text: - Draw a line \( 7 \mathrm{~cm} \) long
- Set the compass width to \( 6 \mathrm{~cm} \) and draw an arc from one end of the line
- Set the compass width to \( 40 \mathrm{~cm} \) and draw an arc from the other end of the line
- Join up the ends of the line to the intersection of the arcs with straight lines
Answer C Text: - Draw a line \( 7 \mathrm{~cm} \) long
- Set the compass width to \( 6 \mathrm{~cm} \) and draw an arc from one end of the line
- Then use the protractor to measure an angle of \( 40^{\circ} \) from the other end of the \( 7 \mathrm{~cm} \) line and place a dot
- Draw a straight line from the end of the line through the dot
- Join up where the arc crosses this line
Answer D Text: - Draw a line \( 7 \mathrm{~cm} \) long
- Place a protractor at one end of the line, measure \( 40^{\circ} \) and place a dot
- Place a protractor at the other end of the line, measure \( 6^{\circ} \) and place a dot
